messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure concerns ClassUtils.getShortClassName() method returning a class name with a trailing semicolon for arrays. The test checks that for a String array, the returned short class name should be "String[]", but the bug report shows it returns "String;".

Examining the method getShortClassName(Class<?> cls), it simply calls cls.getName() and delegates to getShortClassName(String className).

The getShortClassName(String) method handles class names as strings, but the current implementation does not appear to have any special handling for array class names. It directly extracts the last part of the class name based on the package separator character ('.') and replaces inner class '$' with '.'.

Java array class names for object types are encoded in a format starting with '[', and for object arrays including a trailing semicolon after the component type descriptor (for example "[Ljava.lang.String;"). The code currently just treats the class name string as a normal class name without properly decoding the array descriptor.

Hence, when an array class name is passed, the method fails to strip the array descriptor and trailing semicolon properly, causing the returned short name to end with a semicolon.

The test expects the short name for String[].class to be "String[]", but the current implementation returns "String;" due to incorrectly parsing the array type name.

No special code is present in getShortClassName(String) to handle array type names.

Conclusion: The bug occurs because getShortClassName(String) does not handle array type names correctly and leaves the trailing semicolon from the encoded class name string, leading to incorrect short names for arrays.

The fix would involve making getShortClassName(String) detect and decode array type descriptors properly, converting for example "[Ljava.lang.String;" to "String[]", rather than the current naive substring extraction.

Recent bug reports are unrelated and do not provide additional hints.

Final diagnosis:
- The root cause is in ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String) which lacks decoding logic for array class names that are encoded with leading '[' and trailing ';' for object arrays.
- The current naive string manipulation extracts the last dot part but leaves trailing semicolon from the encoded array signature.
- This causes getShortClassName to return "String;" for String[] instead of the expected "String[]".

This explains the test failure and the bug report's symptom of semicolon appended for arrays.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
